My interventions on the process team's favored levers did NOT recover conversion: changes affecting pressure drop, moisture, and bed height (experiments 6 & 8) left conversion unchanged, ruling out the 'too cool / wrong pressure / physical bed' theories. The slightly elevated effluent byproduct fraction is only weakly correlated with conversion (r~0.12), so it is a bystander/decoy, not the driver. The consistent picture is a feed-borne poison deactivating the fixed catalyst bed. Because the direct 'feed guard adsorbent' actuator is not connected on this unit, the fix must use the available feed purification/polishing system to strip the contaminant upstream, combined with catalyst regeneration to restore already-poisoned active sites. Retuning temperature/pressure would waste effort chasing a decoy.
